content.text: {"headline":"Approve P1 (no-cost rebalance): predicted 84.2% service level for 14:30-19:15 against the 80% target, at no extra cost.","why":"The problem is demand, not staffing. The 12:30 credit card limit upgrade SMS (MKT-2026-951) pushed general queue calls to +72% by 13:30, mostly new_offer_enquiry calls at 5.2x normal. Staffing is only about 2 agents below plan. P1 meets the target without spending anything. It delays general breaks 15:00-16:00 by 45 minutes, moves 5 cross-skilled agents from payments to general 17:00-18:00 and 2 agents 19:00-20:00, and offers IVR callback on general 16:00-18:00. Predicted abandons fall to 2.9% (3.3% with no action). Rest of day is 84.3%. The plan follows policy, and no escalation is needed.","trade_offs":["General still sits below target at 78.1%, even though the combined figure is 84.2%. Payments holds up at 91.1% and is not harmed by the agent moves, so the gap on general is the main weak point.","Doing nothing (P0) is also free and gives 82.0% combined. But general would be at 74.3% with 3.3% abandons, which leaves little margin.","P4 gives 88.5% combined and 83.6% on general with no customer-facing changes and no policy issues. It costs INR 2,160 in overtime. Keep it as the fallback if P1 underdelivers.","P2 (86.7%, INR 120) and P3 (91.1%, INR 2,160) break policy CX-01. A known-issue IVR message needs a confirmed outage or incident, and there isn't one, so neither can be used as is."],"watch":"Watch new_offer_enquiry volume and general queue service level, especially 15:00-16:00 while breaks are delayed and 17:00-18:00. If general stays well below 78% or abandons go above 3%, switch to the P4 overtime offers."}
